$comment: CANONICAL registry for the engraved icon set. Markdown mirrors defer to
this file, same convention as design-elements/3d-icons/manifest.json.

meta.name: Engraved icons
meta.style: Monochrome glyph, top-down light: a soft grey vertical gradient with a 4px drop shadow and a 2px inner shadow, so the shape reads as pressed into the surface rather than drawn on it.
meta.status: ASSETS PRESENT, IN USE — not yet an Approved Component
meta.$comment_status: Four glyphs, all live in the first-run flow. They are NOT tier-1 3D icons (those are rendered objects) and NOT tier-2 flat monoline (those are strokes at row scale). This is a third register: a large engraved glyph that carries a page the way a 3D render does, without being a photograph of an object. That distinction is why they get their own folder rather than joining either tier — and it is also an unresolved question for .claude/rules/design-system.md, whose icon gate describes exactly two tiers.
meta.usage: One per page, in the visual half, at 96-104px. Never a row icon.
meta.$comment_embedding: Consumed as base64 data URIs rather than inlined markup: every file carries Figma-generated filter and gradient ids (filter0_di_*, paint0_linear_*), and two screens share the DOM during a transition, so inlining would collide those ids.

icons.conflict: ⚠ The unread dot is #FF4444 at 54% — a red that is NOT in the palette. `red.mid` (#D65151) is the token for exactly this and was what the drawn bell used. Left as supplied because the file is the owner's artwork and re-colouring it silently would hide the divergence; flagged so it can be decided rather than inherited.
